claims.claim: Koray Kavukcuoglu announced Gemini 4 Hydrogen, adapted from Gemini 4 Carbon for speed, and said it surpasses Gemini 4 Argon at its default thinking level.

claims.supporting_quote: Adapted from Gemini 4 Carbon and focused on speed, Google claims that Hydrogen also surpasses its frontier Gemini 4 Argon model when using its default thinking level.

claims.claim: Gemini 4 Hydrogen scored 51 on the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index at its default high thinking level, compared with 50 for Gemini 4 Argon, and 54 at the extra-high setting.
claims.episode_span: a score of 51 on the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index at that default, against 50 for Argon, rising to 54
claims.source_title: Google Launches Gemini 4 Hydrogen for Faster Coding and AI Workflows
claims.supporting_quote: Google said Gemini 4 Hydrogen scored 51 on the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index at its default high thinking level, compared with 50 for Gemini 4 Argon. Its score rises to 54 at the highest extra-high thinking setting.

claims.claim: Google said Hydrogen completes tasks 2.5 times faster than Gemini 3.8 Flash at the default high thinking level and scored 57 percent on Terminal-Bench 4.1 versus 18.2 percent for Gemini 3.8 Flash.

claims.supporting_quote: Compared with Gemini 3.8 Flash , Google said that Hydrogen completes tasks 2.5 times faster at its default high thinking level. It also scored 57% on Terminal-Bench 4.1, compared with 18.2% for Gemini 3.8 Flash.

claims.claim: Google priced Hydrogen at $1.50 per million input tokens and $7.50 per million output tokens across a context window of up to 1 million tokens.

claims.source_title: Google Launches Gemini 4 Hydrogen for Faster Coding and AI Workflows
claims.supporting_quote: Google has priced Hydrogen at $1.50 per million input tokens and $7.50 per million output tokens across its 1-million-token context window.

claims.claim: On Terminal-Bench 4.0, Orchestrator achieved task success rates close to Carbon while using 24 percent less quota and completing tasks 19 percent faster.
claims.episode_span: on Terminal-Bench 4.0, landed near Carbon's success rate while using 24 percent less quota and finishing 19 percent faster
claims.source_title: Google Launches Gemini 4 Hydrogen for Faster Coding and AI Workflows
claims.supporting_quote: On Terminal-Bench 4.0, Orchestrator achieved task success rates close to Carbon while consuming 24% less quota on average and completing tasks 19% faster, Google said.

claims.claim: Google said Hydrogen is two times less likely than Gemini 3.8 Flash to circumvent permission boundaries and is still prone to hallucinations.
claims.episode_span: Hydrogen is two times less likely than 3.8 Flash to step past permission boundaries, and that it still hallucinates
claims.source_title: Google unveils Gemini 4 Hydrogen, its new AI model built for speed
claims.supporting_quote: Compared to 3.8 Flash, Google claims that Hydrogen is two times less likely to circumvent permission boundaries. The company further stated that it's continuing to work on the AI model's safety and security aspects such as jailbreak resistance, though noted that Hydrogen is still prone to hallucinations, like all generative AI agents .

claims.claim: Free Gemini users cannot pick Hydrogen themselves; most prompts still go to Flash-Lite, and with auto selection off every reply comes from Flash-Lite.
claims.episode_span: free users get it only through automatic model selection when Google judges the prompt suitable, that most prompts still go to Flash-Lite

claims.supporting_quote: Free users cannot pick Hydrogen themselves. Google says they get it through auto model selection "when it's the appropriate model for the prompt." The Gemini Apps Help adds that most prompts still go to Flash-Lite and that "prompts that require more reasoning may use Hydrogen." With auto model selection turned off, every reply comes from Flash-Lite.
